artifacts.summary: Four-phase, ~6h plan promoting the research prototype into two new Lean modules (Semantics/BLFrame.lean, Metalogic/Conservativity/SpCountermodel.lean) delivering a native BL frame class, native BL soundness, the two-fibre countermodel, not_derivable_sp and tmCompleteBase_refuted, plus repository record correction.

memory_candidates.content: Pattern for machine-checking an UNDERIVABILITY claim when the target formula is valid throughout the repository's primary semantic class: no countermodel can exist inside that class, so define a MINIMAL NATIVE frame notion outside it (a bare structure with only the order conditions the axioms actually need), give it its own truth recursion (not a reindexing of the existing truth relation), prove soundness of the object proof system against it by recursion on the derivation tree with termination_by height, then evaluate the target there. The native class need not be the intended semantics -- underivability only needs SOME class on which the proof system is sound, and reaching a given axiom by a different route on the new class (e.g. a universal modality underwriting an axiom that the primary semantics underwrites via group structure) is a feature, not a mismatch. Two structural helpers recur: (a) if the new frame class is closed under order reversal, a swap-TRANSFER lemma (truth on the reversed frame iff truth of the syntactically dualized formula) discharges a temporal-duality rule in one line, replacing a swap-strengthened simultaneous induction; (b) refuting a boxed dichotomy needs two order-shapes simultaneously accessible, which is a DISJOINT sum, never a lexicographic one -- a lexicographic sum is still a single linear order. Worked examples in this repo: Metalogic/Conservativity/Z1Countermodel.lean and the (Sp)/CEB two-fibre countermodel over Z (+) R.
